title: TIC monthly release (February 2027 data) — an April REVISION edition on the only structurally FOMC-free slot in the series, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes) by this event's own session — its 2027 table's April row reads '15' in the Monthly column with BOTH quarterly columns EMPTY and '30 - final' standing in the separate 'Annual: Foreign portfolio holdings of U.S. securities at end-June of previous year' column, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. A SINGLE-CUT monthly release; the final annual survey is a distinct release fifteen days later. Reference month February 2027 by the page's own 1.5-month lag rule. Mechanically corroborated EXACTLY: April 2027 carries no 5 U.S.C. 6103 federal holiday and the 11th business day of April 2027 is 2027-04-15 — offset +0 inside the page's '11th business day plus 0 to 3 days' rule. That corroboration is stated as weak in the CONVENTION sense (with no April holiday the holiday-aware and holiday-blind readings coincide, so this date discriminates nothing between them) but strong in the RULE sense, which is new and April-specific: across the twelve published April releases 2015-2026, read off Treasury's own release-date history, TEN land on the 11th business day exactly (+0) and the other two at +1 (2025-04-16) and +2 (2024-04-17) — against 9 exact of 24 across the whole 2026-27 schedule. April is where this rule is nearly deterministic. Promoted estimate -> confirmed by this event's own session per the no-self-confirm limit that filed it (the proposer may not confirm what it found); confirmed describes the published schedule and nothing else, and the same page carries Treasury's closure-revision notice. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: TITLE CORRECTED from the proposal that created this entry (2026-09-09, by tic-monthly-2027-03-18). The proposal filed it as 'the clean-axis test the Feb/Mar exclusion never had', paired to the FINAL annual survey. Both halves are wrong and are corrected here rather than inherited. (1) SEQUENCE: 2027-04-15 stands FIFTEEN DAYS BEFORE the final survey (2027-04-30), so that survey's benchmark cannot reach this edition; the first revision edition after it is 2027-07-16. The survey this edition can carry is the PRELIMINARY one (2027-02-26, 48 days earlier). Treasury's note (d) pairs a monthly release with a survey only for the PRE-SEPTEMBER-2011 regime (March=prelim, May=final) — the same sentence tic-monthly-2027-02-18 used to date that mechanism as retired. This is the THIRD separate-column / sequence misread of this one table in the series (Feb caught the prelim column, March the gross-external-debt column, April the annual column's sequence). (2) AXIS: read off the January sibling's own two printed readings, the revision-edition mean is $5.01bn in BOTH ($5.01 vs $4.46 ordinary, p=0.78, with Feb/Mar left in; $5.01 vs $1.67, p<0.001, with them excluded). February and March are never Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct editions, so every excluded vintage is CONTROL-class and the treatment mean is invariant to the disputed exclusion. One more revision-edition observation therefore cannot discriminate between the two readings — the contested axis is the control, and the correct-axis test is the one tic-monthly-2027-03-18 already registered (FT-tic-monthly-2027-03-18-2, on the ordinary-class Jun/Sep/Dec editions). WHAT THIS EVENT ACTUALLY CARRIES, and it is worth more than the framing it lost. Its corridor is the THINNEST in the series — two tracked events within +/-5 days (opex-2027-04-16, the scored session, and fomc-blackout-start-2027-04-17) against eight for each of the January, February and March siblings and 27 for 2026-12-15. And that is STRUCTURAL, the exact mirror of the March sibling's finding: the April TIC release stands +12 to +21 calendar days before the next FOMC decision in 14 of 14 years 2014-2027, never once inside the +/-2-session contamination window, where March's collides in 12 of 14. Measured on the same 2,990 sessions: zero of 93 monthly (non-quarterly) opex sessions fall within two sessions of an FOMC, against 32 of 47 quad-witchings — so this scored session's class is clean by construction of the two calendars. So this ledger REGISTERS a TIC-keyed tape test, the first since 2027-01-19: March refused it, April restores it. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds (16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, the data is six weeks stale, no house playbook is macro-keyed). Nothing here licenses an entry.
